bilingual.notes: NC has no separate 'bilingual education' teaching license. The Elementary (K-6) Second Language add-on (valid for full-time assignments in grades 6 and below) and the K-12 'Other Second Languages' world-language licenses are the closest analogs. NC operates 300+ Dual Language/Immersion programs in 8 languages, staffed by teachers who hold content-area licenses plus appropriate language qualifications.

eld.notes: ESL is offered both as a K-12 standalone license (Special Subjects) and as a K-6 add-on to Elementary licensure. Approved educator preparation program (traditional or alternative) is the route to licensure; Praxis II ESL has been the state-required licensure exam for this area since 2003 (current administration via Pearson/ETS per SBE policy LICN-003).

history.title: NC Professional Teaching Standards adopted (still operative)
history.description: The State Board of Education adopted the NC Professional Teaching Standards in 2007 (revised 2008) and they remain the operative standards document. Standard II ("diverse population of students"), Standard IV references to language proficiency, and pervasive cultural-diversity language ground the schema's `professionalStandardsMentions.{diverse, cultural, linguistic}: true`. The standards do not name "English learner" or "EL" explicitly, holding `el: false`.

history.title: North Carolina adopts Seal of Biliteracy (Global Languages Endorsement)
history.description: NC adopted the Seal of Biliteracy in 2015, implemented as the Global Languages Endorsement on the high school diploma. Recognizes graduates who demonstrate proficiency in English and at least one other world language. Per the schema, this is a student-side credential and is recorded as context — the closest teacher-side analog (K-6 "Second Language" add-on) remains separate.

history.title: EPAA 29(100) document analysis (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021)
history.description: Leider, Colombo & Nerlino published in Education Policy Analysis Archives 29(100) a comprehensive document analysis of every state and DC's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI teacher-credentialing requirements, professional teaching standards mentions, and EL-percentage figures, based on primary SEA sources collected October–December 2019. The 2019 coding of North Carolina's EL-credentialing landscape is preserved as a temporally-anchored research baseline against which the catalog's later verifications are framed.

elPercentHistory.note: North Carolina Department of Public Instruction, November 1 headcount (178,688 EL students of 1,504,424 ADM). In December 2024, the State Board of Education lowered the EL exit threshold from 4.8 to 4.5 and mandated a single statewide screener replacing district-by-district screening; the November 2024 figure reflects pending implementation of these changes, which limits direct comparability to NCES's fall 2021 figure (8.0%) beyond the documented enrollment growth. North Carolina does not publish a multi-year EL series for fall 2018-2021 in directly accessible form, so methodological continuity with the prior NCES series cannot be confirmed from overlapping observations.
